threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, roles, and timeline for the budgeting process rollout.

messages.text:
Kicking off the rollout of our standardized budgeting and forecasting process for the next planning cycle. The goal is to have a unified way of building budgets and cash-flow forecasts across all units, with clear roles and timelines.

Scope wise, this should cover: documented end to end process, standard chart of accounts mapping, 12 month rolling cash-flow forecast template, monthly budget vs actual reporting, internal control checklist, and training materials.

To get there, we will rely on the tasks already defined, especially T1 for mapping current practices and T6 for the governance and approval workflow. Later on, A3 will consolidate the full process.

Can each of you confirm your responsibilities and flag any constraints for the next three weeks, so we can lock scope and milestones?

Thanks for starting this. I can take T1 and later T10, and also support with T8 once we are closer to training.

My main constraint is that I am helping with some admin work around month end, so interviews or surveys for T1 will be easier if we avoid the last three days of the month. I will start drafting a simple questionnaire to capture current templates, timelines, and pain points.

Before I move, can you confirm which departments are in scope for T1 so I do not miss anyone?

From my side, I will own T2, T5, T7, and T11. I will also review the materials for T8.

Key constraint is that during month end close I will have limited time for workshops, but I can still review drafts async. For the process description in A3, I suggest we keep a running outline so we do not leave documentation to the very end.

Once T1 gives us the current templates and pain points, I will start a first draft of the standard budget template and the internal control checklist, then sync with the financial managers for approvals and compliance checks.

I will take T4 as main owner and support on data aspects for T5 and T9 when needed.

On constraints: reconciliation for the last 12 months will be heavy if we overlap with close. If we want a clean baseline for the first cycle, I recommend we agree on which ledgers and periods are mandatory for go live, and which can be improved later.

Once we agree on that, I will prepare the baseline dataset and store it in the shared location so it can feed the forecast model and the budget vs actual reports.

I can focus on T3, T6, T9, and T12, and help validate assumptions and governance.

I will need some support from you all to make sure the model and workflow fit with our current accounting exports and reporting cadence. I also want to avoid clashes with month end, so for T6 and T9 we should schedule workshops outside the close window.

Once we have clarity from T1 and T4, I will propose a first version of the cash-flow model and a draft of the approval workflow for review.

For T1, let us include at least: all business unit leads, finance, and any area that currently submits a budget or forecast, even informally. If you are unsure about a specific team, add them to the survey and we can decide based on responses.

Please also capture how they currently use any budget vs actual views, so we can feed that into the reporting package and A3 later.

Got it. I will prepare a short survey today and share a draft here before sending it out, to make sure I am not missing any key questions.

I will also add a section on how they track budget vs actual today and what tools they use, so we can align with the future reporting package.

When you share the survey draft, I will add a couple of questions on chart of accounts mapping and any off system spreadsheets they maintain. That will help me design the standard template and avoid surprises later.

Once T1 is done, I will start filling an outline for A3 with the future state process, so we can iterate as we go.

On the baseline, my suggestion is to prioritize the main revenue and expense ledgers plus bank and key balance sheet accounts for the last 12 months. That should be enough to test the 12 month forecast and the budget vs actual package.

If we agree, I will flag any material inconsistencies to the accountant as I go, so we can decide whether they need corrections before go live or can be handled as one off adjustments.

That approach works for me. If you can tag the inconsistencies by type and period, I can quickly assess impact on the reporting and on compliance.

For anything that could affect tax or statutory reporting, I will review in detail and record the conclusion in the channel, so we have a clear trail for T11 later.

On T6, I am thinking of a simple three step flow: department submission, finance review, and final approval by the finance director or delegate. We can add escalation rules for late submissions.

I will draft this and share for comments. If anyone sees a risk with our current tools or timing, please flag so we can adjust before we lock the timeline.

On scope, I propose we keep the first rollout cycle focused on: the standard budget template, the 12 month cash-flow model, the monthly budget vs actual package, and a basic but complete version of A3 and the internal control checklist. Training materials can be light for the first cycle and expanded after the pilot.

Anything beyond that, like automation or system changes, we can treat as a later phase.

If no one objects by tomorrow, I will consider this the agreed scope for the first cycle.

Scope sounds reasonable to me, especially keeping automation for later. That should make it easier to get buy in from departments in the first round.

No objections from my side.

Agreed on the scope. With that, I can prioritize the template, reporting package, and controls, and keep the documentation in A3 evolving as we learn from the pilot.

I will also make sure the checklist covers the key tax and reporting points we need for the first cycle.

No objections from me either. Keeping the first cycle focused on templates, model, reporting, and basic controls makes sense.

On timeline, given the 21 day window and month end constraints, I suggest we target: week 1 for T1 and T4, week 2 for T2, T3, and T6 drafts, and week 3 for review, adjustments, and preparing for the pilot.

The proposed timeline works for T4 as long as we confirm which ledgers and periods are in scope this week. That way I can plan reconciliation work around close.

If we lock that today or tomorrow, I can start pulling data and flagging issues by mid week.

I like the three week structure. To make it explicit:

Week 1: T1 and T4
Week 2: T2, T3, T6
Week 3: review, finalize A3 draft, and prepare for pilot planning.

If everyone is ok with this, we will treat it as our baseline timeline and adjust only if close activities force changes.
Timeline works for me. I will aim to complete the T1 survey and initial interviews within week 1 so that templates and governance can build on real feedback.

Aligned on the timeline. I will block some time in week 2 to work on T2, T5, and T7, and keep A3 updated as we go.

If we see any risk of slippage due to close, we can raise it in the twice weekly async check in and adjust.

threads.thread_goal: Design and finalize the standard budget and cash-flow templates.

messages.text:
I have uploaded the first draft of the standard budget template, based on inputs from T1 and our current chart of accounts. This is A1, version 1.

Structure:
- Income section by main revenue lines
- Operating expenses by nature
- Simple balance sheet items for key working capital accounts

Fields are mapped to the existing chart of accounts so we can tie back to the ledger. For now, I kept the level of detail moderate to avoid overwhelming departments.

Can you review and comment on whether the structure and granularity work for your areas before we lock it for the first cycle?

Thanks for sharing A1. From a finance lead perspective, the structure looks clear. My main question is whether we need more breakdown on operating expenses for the first cycle, for example separating marketing, personnel, and overheads, or if we keep it higher level and refine later.

Also, can you confirm that the template will work with the monthly budget vs actual report in A5 without extra manual mapping?

I went through A1 and the mapping to the chart of accounts looks consistent with how we post in the ledger.

For expenses, I would recommend at least separating personnel, rent, utilities, and marketing. That will make variance analysis more meaningful later in A5 without adding too much complexity.

From a data perspective, this structure should be easy to reconcile with the baseline once T4 is done.

Looking at A1 from a user perspective, the layout is straightforward. For the training materials in T8, it will help if we keep the number of mandatory fields clear and add short explanations for each section.

One question: do we expect departments to input balance sheet items directly, or will those be derived from other assumptions in the cash-flow model?

For the first cycle, I would prefer to keep balance sheet inputs in A1 limited to items that have a clear link to cash, like receivables, payables, and inventory. We can then use those to feed the 12 month cash-flow model in A2.

More complex balance sheet projections can wait for a later phase once we see how departments handle the basics.

On the expense breakdown, I can adjust A1 to show at least personnel, rent, utilities, marketing, and other operating expenses. That should still be manageable for departments.

Regarding A5, I have aligned the codes so that we can pull actuals by the same groupings. Once T4 provides the reconciled baseline, we can test a pilot month to confirm there is no extra manual mapping needed.

For balance sheet, I will follow the suggestion and keep only key working capital items as inputs in A1. The rest we can handle centrally when we build the cash-flow model in A2.

I will also add short field descriptions in the template so that T8 can reuse that wording in the user guide.

Switching to the cash-flow side, I have started outlining A2 based on our main cash in and cash out categories.

For cash in: customer receipts, other income, and financing inflows.
For cash out: supplier payments, payroll, taxes, capex, and debt service.

I propose we assume standard payment terms of 30 days for customers and 30 days for suppliers for the first cycle, unless a unit has a clearly different pattern. Seasonality can be handled by monthly percentage adjustments.

Please let me know if these categories and assumptions work, or if we need more granularity from day one.

The categories in A2 cover the main cash movements we see in the ledger. For payment terms, 30 days is a good default, but we should allow overrides for units with longer customer terms or specific supplier agreements.

For seasonality, a simple monthly factor per revenue and key expense category should be enough for the first cycle. We can refine later if we see big deviations.

From a management view, those categories and assumptions are acceptable for the first cycle. I would just ask that we document the default terms and seasonality approach clearly in A7 so that everyone understands how the forecast is built.

We can then revisit the assumptions in T12 once we have a few months of actuals.

For training, it will help if A2 has a simple input section for assumptions and a separate section for the calculated forecast. That way, in T8 and A6 we can show users exactly where to adjust payment terms or seasonality without touching formulas.

Good point on overrides. I will set 30 days as the default in A2 but add optional fields for specific customer or supplier groups where units can input different terms.

I will also structure the model so that assumptions are clearly separated from calculations, as suggested, to make training easier.

Given the feedback so far, I will update A1 to:
- Add the suggested expense breakdown
- Limit balance sheet inputs to key working capital items
- Include short field descriptions

Unless there are strong objections, I suggest we treat this structure and level of detail as final for the first rollout cycle, and only adjust after the pilot feedback in A8.

I am comfortable treating the updated A1 structure as final for the first cycle. The breakdown and working capital focus should give us enough insight without overcomplicating things.

We can log any improvement ideas during the pilot in A8.

On the cash-flow side, I propose we confirm the following for the first cycle:
- Cash in categories: customer receipts, other income, financing inflows
- Cash out categories: suppliers, payroll, taxes, capex, debt service
- Default payment terms: 30 days for customers and suppliers, with overrides where needed
- Seasonality handled via monthly percentage factors

If everyone agrees, we can record these as the standard assumptions in A7 and use them in A2.
Those categories and assumptions work for me and match what we see in the books. Having them documented in A7 will also help when we reconcile forecast vs actual later.

Agreed. Once you finalize A2 with these assumptions, I will cross check that the budget template A1 and the reporting template A5 align with the same categories, so we have a consistent chain from budget to forecast to actuals.

threads.thread_goal: Resolve data quality issues and confirm the baseline dataset.

messages.text:
Quick update on T4. I have reconciled the main revenue and expense ledgers plus bank accounts for the last 12 months. Most months tie out, but I found a few inconsistencies:
- Two months with unmatched revenue entries due to missing customer codes
- Some expense reclassifications that were posted late

I have a draft list of these items ready to share. Before I finalize the baseline dataset, we need to decide which periods and ledgers are mandatory for the first cycle so we do not delay the project.

I suggest we use the last 12 closed months for P and L and bank, and focus on the main working capital accounts for the balance sheet. Thoughts?

Thanks for the summary. For the unmatched revenue entries, can you share the amounts and months? I need to check if they could affect tax or statutory reporting.

For the first cycle, I agree that last 12 closed months for P and L and bank are the minimum. For balance sheet, receivables, payables, and inventory should be enough to support the cash-flow model and the budget vs actual report in A5.

From a forecasting perspective, having 12 months of clean P and L and bank data is important to test A2 and the reporting in A5.

If some items are small and do not affect trends, we can document them and move on. For anything material, we should at least understand the impact, even if we cannot correct everything before go live.

I support focusing on the last 12 closed months and the key ledgers you mentioned. We should not let older or less relevant data block the rollout.

Can you also confirm where you will store the baseline dataset so that we can reference it in A3 and use it for the pilot?

The unmatched revenue entries total is small relative to monthly revenue, but I will send you a short list with amounts and months so you can assess any tax impact.

For the baseline, I can prepare a consolidated file with 12 months of P and L, bank, and the main working capital accounts, and store it in our shared finance folder. I will also tag it clearly as the baseline for this project.

Perfect. Once I have the list of unmatched entries, I will review them and record in the channel whether they require corrections or can be treated as immaterial for T11.

For the baseline file, please include clear column headers and a short tab explaining any adjustments you made, so that when we build A5 we know exactly what we are comparing against.

Once the baseline is in place, I will use it to test A2 with the last 6 months of actual data, as required in T3. That will help us see if the cash-flow assumptions we agreed in A7 produce reasonable results.

So having the baseline ready soon will unblock that step.

Given the time constraints, I propose we formally define the baseline as:
- Last 12 closed months of P and L and bank ledgers
- Receivables, payables, and inventory balances for the same period

Older periods or less material ledgers can be cleaned later without affecting the first rollout.

If there are no objections, we will treat this as the agreed baseline scope.

That definition matches what I have already reconciled, so I am fine with using it as the baseline for this project.

I will finalize the file with those ledgers and periods and share the link in this channel.

Agreed on the baseline scope. For the unmatched and late entries, I will document in a short note whether they affect the comparability of the budget vs actual report in A5, so we know how to interpret variances in the first months.

No objections from me. With that baseline, we can move ahead with testing A2 and preparing the pilot reporting in A5.

If we discover any major issues during the pilot, we can log them in A8 and adjust for the next cycle.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and execute the pilot with one business unit and capture feedback.

messages.text:
With the templates and baseline coming together, we should plan the pilot for the new process.

I propose we run the pilot with one business unit that has relatively stable operations and good data discipline, so we can focus on testing A1, A2, and A5 rather than firefighting.

My initial thought is to use the main services unit, as they already submit informal budgets and have fewer one off transactions. We could target next month for them to submit their budget using A1 and for us to produce a 12 month cash-flow forecast in A2 and a budget vs actual report in A5.

What do you think about this unit and timing?

The main services unit is a good candidate. They are usually responsive and already work with simple forecasts.

On timing, we need to avoid the month end close week. If we ask them to submit their budget in the first half of next month, we can then use the second half to run the cash-flow and reporting and collect feedback.

From a template and reporting angle, the services unit is manageable and should give us a clear view of how A1 and A5 perform in practice.

I would like to sit in on their first run through the template, even if just on a short call, to see where they hesitate or ask questions. That will feed directly into improvements for A6 and the control checklist.

Data wise, the services unit is one of the cleaner ones, so it is a good choice for the pilot. Their historical data is already in the baseline from T4, which will make it easier to compare forecast vs actual.

I can support by checking that their submitted A1 ties back to the ledger and by helping prepare the pilot budget vs actual report in A5.

For training and communication, starting with the services unit is also easier. I can adapt the draft materials from T8 and A6 to their context and run a short intro session before they fill A1.

We should also plan how we will capture their feedback systematically in A8 so we do not lose any insights.

Based on your feedback, I suggest we formalize the pilot plan as:
- Pilot unit: main services business unit
- Budget submission using A1: by the 10th of next month
- Cash-flow forecast in A2 and budget vs actual report in A5: by the 20th of next month
- Feedback session and logging in A8: by the end of the month

If everyone agrees, we can inform the unit manager and lock these dates.

I am aligned with that plan. I will reach out to the services unit manager to confirm their availability and explain the expectations for the pilot.

Once they confirm, we can treat the dates as fixed and adjust only if there is a major conflict.
Works for me. I will plan to review their A1 submission shortly after the 10th and prepare a draft A5 for the services unit so we can show them how their data flows through the process.

I will schedule a short training session with the services unit before the 10th and tailor the T8 materials and A6 guide to their examples.

During the session, I will note any questions or confusion so we can log them in A8 later.
I will be ready to support with data checks once the services unit submits A1. After we produce A5 for them, I can compare it against the baseline from T4 to see if there are any unexpected gaps.

For the pilot feedback, I propose we structure A8 with three sections:
- Template usability (A1 and A2)
- Reporting clarity (A5)
- Process and timing (T6 and T9)

During the feedback session, we can capture comments under these headings and then decide which changes we implement before the full rollout.

I like that structure. For template usability, I will pay attention to any repeated issues, like confusion about fields or missing categories, and propose concrete tweaks to A1 and A2.

For reporting clarity, we can ask the unit whether the A5 view helps them manage their budget or if they need additional breakdowns.

I will prepare a simple feedback form aligned with those three sections and share it with the services unit after the session. That way we have both live discussion notes and written comments to store in A8.

Once we have the feedback consolidated in A8, we should agree which changes are mandatory before full rollout and which can wait.

My suggestion is to prioritize fixes that affect understanding of the templates or reports, and leave cosmetic or nice to have items for later.

Agreed. After the pilot, we will review A8 and decide on a small set of changes to A1, A2, A5, or the process in T6 that we implement before go live.

We will treat other suggestions as backlog for future cycles so we do not delay the rollout.

Makes sense. I will focus my post pilot changes on clarifying fields, fixing any mapping issues, and updating the internal control checklist where needed. Anything beyond that can go into a later improvement round.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize controls, documentation, and training before full rollout.

messages.text:
I have put together a first draft of the process document in A3 and the training materials for T8.

A3 currently covers:
- High level overview of the budgeting and forecasting cycle
- Roles and responsibilities by task (T1 to T12)
- Timelines and key milestones

For training, I created a slide deck explaining the new process and deadlines, plus a one page quick reference guide aligned with A6.

Can you review and let me know what is missing, especially around internal controls and compliance points?

Thanks for the draft. I have also prepared a first version of the internal control checklist in A4 for T7.

It covers:
- Data entry checks for A1 and A2
- Review steps for variances in A5
- Sign off points for key approvals

I will review A3 and your training materials to make sure the controls are reflected consistently. We also need to ensure that tax and statutory requirements are clearly addressed for T11.

I went through A3 and the training deck. The overall flow is clear. I would suggest adding a short section on how we will review forecast assumptions quarterly as part of T12, so people know this is not a one off exercise.

Also, in the training, it might help to show a simple example of how a department budget in A1 ends up in the cash-flow model A2 and the report A5.

From a data and control perspective, A4 looks solid. I would just add a step to confirm that the baseline dataset from T4 is used consistently when preparing the first budget vs actual reports in A5, so we avoid confusion about starting points.

In A3, maybe we can include a short note on how data issues will be escalated and resolved during the cycle.

Overall, the documentation and training look on track. Before we sign off, I want to be sure that:
- A4 clearly states who signs off at each step
- A3 reflects the final governance from T6
- The training materials in T8 and A6 are simple enough for non finance managers

Once we confirm these points and the compliance review in T11 is done, I am comfortable approving for go live.

I will update A4 to make the sign off responsibilities explicit for each control and cross check that they match the governance defined in T6.

For T11, I have already reviewed the key tax related assumptions and statutory reporting requirements. I will add a short compliance note to A3 and confirm in this channel once it is done so we have a clear record.

I will add a section in A3 describing the quarterly review of assumptions under T12 and update the training deck to include a simple end to end example from A1 through A2 to A5.

For A6, I will keep the language as plain as possible and highlight only the key actions and deadlines for managers.

Once you finalize A4 and the compliance note in A3, I can do a quick pass to ensure the data related steps are practical given how we work today, especially around reconciliations and variance explanations.

Compliance review for T11 is now complete. I have checked the main tax related assumptions, statutory reporting links, and sign off points.

I added a short section in A3 summarizing the key compliance considerations and updated A4 to reference them where relevant.

From my side, the controls and documentation are ready for approval.

I have reviewed the updated A3, A4, and the training materials. The roles, timelines, and controls are clear, and the quarterly review in T12 is now well described.

I do not see any remaining gaps from a process perspective.

I have also refined the training deck and A6 based on your feedback and the pilot experience. The quick reference guide now points directly to the key steps in A3 and the main controls in A4.

Unless there are objections, I think T8 and T10 can be considered complete for the first rollout.

Given the updates:
- A4 now has clear sign off responsibilities
- A3 reflects the final governance from T6 and includes the compliance note and quarterly review
- Training materials in T8 and A6 are aligned and tested with the pilot unit

I am comfortable signing off on the internal controls, documentation, and training plan for go live.

Let us treat this as the formal approval for the first full rollout cycle.

Great. I will archive the current versions of A3, A4, A5, and A6 as the baseline set for this rollout and note in the channel that any further changes will go through a controlled update process after the first full cycle.
